name: impruve
description: The Impruve agent skills, for repos built on the Impruve shared infrastructure.

plugins.name: impruve
plugins.description: Skills for the Impruve gates + review pipeline: /impruve:ship takes a branch through PR, gates, review, and the ticket's QA plan — which it executes against the running stack, writing one when the ticket has none — fixes the findings, then decides once: auto-merge when clean, or hold for a human; /impruve:qa QAs a focus area against the running stack then hands the fixes to ship; /impruve:bugfix turns a specific bug report into a merged fix — reproducing it before touching code, fixing at the layer the invariant belongs, remediating already-corrupted data, then handing off to ship. /impruve:gather-requirements settles what a ticket or an initiative is actually asking for — investigating the code and the decision records before it asks anything, interviewing until the picture is complete, then writing back a description that stands on its own and, for an initiative, its feature definitions. It writes no plans. /impruve:plan-ticket takes it from there — investigating the code at file-and-line level, then writing back a file-anchored implementation plan and an executable QA plan. /impruve:plan-initiative plans a whole initiative by running plan-ticket over each of its tickets in build order, injecting each one's place in the sequence and what the earlier plans decided. /impruve:assess-risk rates a ticket against the engineering-risk rubric the tracker declares — reading the criteria out of the tool rather than carrying a copy, going and looking at the code each one asks about, then writing back one level and one specific rationale per criterion. It is advisory: it refuses nothing, moves nothing, and writes no other field. /impruve:implement-ticket takes a groomed ticket the rest of the way — checking its plan still matches the code, building it, executing its QA plan against the running stack, then handing off to ship. /impruve:just-do-it is the fast path for work already thought through — checking the ticket really is small, then building and shipping it in one session rather than three skills, and handing it back when it turns out not to be. /impruve:author-skill creates or cleans up a skill in any repo to Impruve's standards, testing it the way users run it and handing off a report.
